answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with cross-branch quorum: minting a durable identity requires concurrent approvals from three protocol branches that keep disjoint histories. Each branch deposits a pigment hash of the applicant's prior attestations into a shared vault; only when the vault holds matching ivory-tier seals from all three branches does the mint finalize. Cloning on one fork cannot forge the other branches' pigment proofs, so cheap replica swarms fail the vault check and never gain privileges.
